We need to determine number of methyl (CH3) groups in the sample's molecule. We have no direct description of molecule. We can get NMR spectra to infer. Use proton NMR to see signals for CH3 (singlet, doublet, etc). Could also use carbon NMR. Probably easiest: get proton NMR and count distinct CH3 signals? But need number of methyl groups, not distinct signals. Could be overlapping. Might need HSQC to map.

We have no SMILES. So we must measure proton NMR. Use tool proton_nmr_spectra(). Then analyze peaks: methyl groups appear around 0.9 ppm (alkyl) up to maybe 3 ppm if attached to heteroatom. Need to count number of CH3 groups. The spectrum will list peaks with integration values. Integration indicates number of protons. So count total protons in methyl groups: integration for each CH3 peak divided by 3 gives number of methyl groups. Could be overlapping peaks.

Let's get proton NMR.
